AppMainSection.subtitle: From a sentence to a shipped product.
AppMainSection.description: Turbo AI is a build-and-delivery company working at the frontier of AI. Describe what you need — an agent, a data pipeline, an entire product — and we design it, build it and ship it to production.

mission.title: Mission
mission.content: To collapse the distance between an idea and a working product, so that the only limit on what a company can build is what it can imagine.

vision.title: Vision
vision.content: A world where building software is no longer the bottleneck — where any team, in any industry, can go from a sentence to a shipped product at turbo speed.

build.title: What we build
build.description: If you can describe it, we can build it. In practice, the work tends to take one of these six shapes.
build.item_agents_description: Autonomous agents that do real work — research, outreach, operations, customer support — with the guardrails to run unsupervised.
build.item_interfaces_description: Chat and voice interfaces people actually want to use, on the web, on mobile and inside the messaging apps your customers already live in.
build.item_pipelines_description: Ingestion, labelling and evaluation — the unglamorous plumbing that quietly decides whether a model works in production.
build.item_models_description: Fine-tuning, distillation and serving, adapted to your domain and run on hardware you control.
build.item_products_description: Design, front end, back end and deployment. We hand over something real that your customers can use, not a slide deck.
build.item_automation_description: Tools and workflows that remove the repetitive parts of how your team already works, without asking them to change how they work.

process.title: How we build
process.step_1_description: One call to understand the problem. You get back a plan, a timeline and a fixed price, usually within a week.
process.step_2_description: A working prototype in weeks, not quarters. You use it with real data and we adjust until it earns its place.
process.step_3_description: Production deployment on your infrastructure, with documentation, a proper handover and a team that stays reachable.
process.cta_description: Tell us what it is. If we are not the right people to build it, we will say so on the first call.

story.title: How we got here
story.description: Short version: we kept meeting teams who had the idea but not the people to build it.
story.milestone_1_description: Two engineers kept noticing the same thing. The hard part of an AI product was never the model — it was everything around it. The data, the evaluation, the interface, the deployment. Plenty of teams had the idea. Far fewer had the people who could build it.
story.milestone_2_description: We started Turbo AI in Shanghai to be those people. A company built for one purpose: take an idea in, hand a working product back, without the layers that usually sit between the two.
story.milestone_3_description: We build for startups and enterprises across Shanghai and Tokyo. The work has grown and so has what we can deliver. Every engineer here ships production code, and that is deliberate.

news.title: Nothing to report yet
news.description: We have been heads-down building. When there is something worth writing up, it will appear here.

solutions.title: Anything you can describe
solutions.description: We are an engineering company that builds and delivers AI products for other companies. Here is the work in more detail, and how it usually starts.
solutions.outcome_1_description: Running in production, on your infrastructure, used by real people.
solutions.outcome_2_description: Yours to keep, read and change. Handed over with documentation.
solutions.outcome_3_description: We do not disappear at handover. Most clients come back for the next build.

products.title: Things we built for ourselves
products.description: Tools we needed often enough that we turned them into products. They are also the building blocks underneath most of the client work we do.
products.item_chat_description: An agent platform for building, evaluating and deploying conversational products, with the retrieval and guardrail layers already solved.
products.item_label_description: Data labelling and evaluation for teams who need to know whether a model is actually getting better, not just different.
products.item_voice_description: Text to speech and voice interfaces, tuned for languages and accents the big providers tend to handle badly.
products.item_reel_description: Automated video assembly and mixing for teams producing more content than a human editor can keep up with.
products.cta_title: Want one of these adapted to your business?
products.cta_description: Every product here started as client work. We are happy to do that again.

Faq.title: Questions we get asked
Faq.question_1: What does Turbo AI actually do?
Faq.answer_1: We build and deliver AI products for other companies. You describe the problem, we design and build the system, and we deploy it on your infrastructure. Agents, data pipelines, interfaces, whole products — whatever the problem turns out to need.
Faq.answer_2: A working prototype usually takes two weeks. A production system takes four to twelve, depending on how much of your existing infrastructure it has to touch and how strict your compliance requirements are.
Faq.answer_3: You do. Code, models and documentation are handed over and deployed on infrastructure you control. We do not hold your product hostage, and we do not resell your work to anyone else.
Faq.answer_4: The founders and our own AI engineers. There are no layers of account management, and the work is not quietly passed down to people you have never met.
Faq.question_5: What if we already have an engineering team?
Faq.answer_5: Then we work alongside them. A lot of our work is unblocking an in-house team that has hit something unfamiliar, rather than replacing anyone.

career.title: Join the builders
career.description: We hire people who ship AI systems with customers — not slide decks. If you want to build production agents, models and infrastructure that land in the real world, talk to us.

fde.title: Forward deployed engineer (FDE)
fde.description: You sit with the customer, own the outcome and ship working AI systems into production. FDEs at Turbo AI are the sharp end of the build — discovery, design, implementation and handover, often in weeks rather than quarters.
responsibilities: Embed with customer teams to turn ambiguous business problems into shippable AI products.
Design and build end-to-end systems: agents, RAG pipelines, evaluation harnesses and the product surface around them.
Own delivery from first workshop to production cutover, including hardening, observability and documentation.
Work directly with founders and AI engineers to pull the right platform capabilities into each engagement.
Leave the customer with something that runs without you — clear runbooks, metrics and a path to iterate.
requirements: Strong full-stack engineering instincts — you can own both the product surface and the AI plumbing.
Comfort working on-site or closely with customers; you communicate clearly under ambiguity.
Hands-on experience shipping LLM or agent systems (RAG, tool use, evaluation, prompt and context design).
Proficiency in TypeScript and/or Python; familiarity with modern web stacks (e.g. Next.js) is a plus.
Bias to ship: you prefer a working system in production over a perfect design doc.
nice: Prior consulting, solutions engineering or forward-deployed experience.
Domain depth in one of our engagement areas (ops, content, data platforms, internal tools).
Experience handing systems over to customer engineering teams.
fde.closing: If you want to build at the customer edge and see your work land in production fast, this is the role.

ai_engineer.title: AI engineer
ai_engineer.description: You design and build the intelligence layer of the products we ship — agents, model integrations, retrieval, evaluation and the product logic that makes them reliable. You care as much about behaviour in production as about clever prompts.
responsibilities: Design agent architectures, tool interfaces and RAG systems for real customer workloads.
Build evaluation harnesses, regression suites and quality gates so we know when a system is good enough to ship.
Integrate frontier and open models; choose the right stack for latency, cost and quality trade-offs.
Partner with FDEs to land capabilities in customer environments and iterate from production signal.
Contribute reusable patterns back into our internal builder toolkit.
requirements: Solid software engineering background with production experience beyond notebooks.
Deep familiarity with LLM application patterns: prompting, tool calling, RAG, agents and evaluation.
Strong Python skills; TypeScript experience is welcome.
Ability to debug non-deterministic systems — traces, evals, failure modes and cost.
Comfort working in short delivery cycles with clear ownership.
nice: Experience with vector databases, orchestration frameworks or custom agent runtimes.
Background in applied ML, information retrieval or multimodal systems.
Open-source contributions or public writing on LLM systems.
ai_engineer.closing: If you want to build AI that customers actually run — not demos — we want to hear from you.

ai_infra.title: AI infrastructure engineer
ai_infra.description: You build the platform that lets our builders ship faster and more safely — model serving, GPU and cluster operations, observability, CI/CD for AI workloads and the internal tools behind every engagement.
responsibilities: Design and operate model serving, batch and realtime inference paths across cloud and customer environments.
Own containerisation, Kubernetes and infrastructure-as-code for AI workloads.
Build monitoring, tracing and cost controls for LLM and agent systems in production.
Partner with AI engineers and FDEs to harden deployments and shorten time-to-production.
Improve the shared platform: templates, pipelines and developer experience for the build team.
requirements: 2+ years operating production systems; ML or LLM serving experience strongly preferred.
Proficiency in Python and/or Go; comfort with Terraform, Docker and Kubernetes.
Experience with cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, Alibaba Cloud or similar).
Familiarity with CI/CD, observability and reliability practices for data or ML systems.
Clear written communication — you document what you build so others can run it.
nice: Hands-on with Ray, KubeFlow, Triton, vLLM or similar serving stacks.
Experience managing GPU fleets or multi-tenant inference.
Prior work on developer platforms or internal MLOps tooling.
ai_infra.closing: If you like making AI systems reliable at scale so builders can move faster, this is your seat.
